newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Chinese ship carrying 109 being towed to Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Chinese ship carrying 109 being towed to Bermuda.

text.p: A U.S. Coast Guard cutter was towing a crippled Chinese ship carrying 109 people through heavy seas toward Bermuda on Sunday, but the fate of those aboard was uncertain, the Bermuda government said.

The cargo ship Xing Da, suspected of trying to smuggle illegal migrants into the United States, was not expected to reach Hamilton until midday on Tuesday, Quinton Edness, minister of labor, home affairs and public safety, said in a statement.
The ship was found drifting about 150 miles (240 km) off Bermuda by the Coast Guard. The 83 passengers and 26 crew members had been aboard since June and were dehydrated, officials said.
The Coast Guard flew water to the ship, but there were adequate food supplies aboard, and no one required emergency medical attention, officials said.
Edness said the vessel was being towed at a speed of three knots through six-foot (two-meter) swells and was about 140 miles (225 km) west of Bermuda on Sunday morning.
Bermuda was asked to assist the ship because it was in danger on the high seas, and the British colony was obliged to respond under the terms of international conventions, Edness said.
He added that the United States had given assurances that the passengers and crew would remain the responsibility of the U.S. government.

"The Bermuda government has made it clear that none of those aboard the vessel will be formally landed in Bermuda. They will remain at all times under the control of U.S. authorities," Edness said in the statement.
He said the ship's crew had intended to land the 83 passengers, including six women, illegally in the United States.
Observers here noted that because of Bermuda's status, any requests for asylum by the alleged illegal migrants would have to be handled in London.
The Coast Guard was treating its operation as a rescue because of the poor weather and a lack of life rafts and vests aboard the ship, officials said.
The Coast Guard said it could not comment on the ultimate fate of the migrants and crew.
